## S51 — Games and Review flow

**State:** IMPLEMENTED, UNCOMMITTED on `hardening` above `f131394`, following S50. H-23: PASS for per-game error markup, build progress and Cancel, verdict-first review, unscored-position copy, refusal reason/remedy, and paste preservation; a real minutes-long build with Cancel and a real refusal from a live session are NOT_RUN.

### What was done and why

The Games screen already validated every pasted slot and named the first illegal move with game, move, and SAN. S51 moved the badge and error line into `PasteValidation`, so the exact per-game message has its own renderer test instead of living untested inside the bridge-bound screen.

Review now owns its status presentation. `ReviewProgress` renders the S35 scored-of-total text, a native `<progress>` element, and the Cancel control; Cancel is disabled while the request is in flight. `RefusalPanel` renders a reason-specific heading, the coverage numbers when present, and the remedy the builder supplied. Timeline no longer carries a generic "No report for this session" block; it draws the trace and lets Review state the reason.

A valid report opens with `VerdictLine` first. Its existing engine note names how many positions were unscored and why. A failed build keeps its one-sentence error panel; a refused build shows the real reason and remedy and keeps Edit games, Back to session, Home, and Help available. The paste draft remains in the reducer through Games -> Review -> Games, and opening a stored session also loads its PGNs into the same draft.

When an older session is opened, the renderer now adopts that session id before the build, so progress events and insight requests target the opened session rather than the last live one. Focus also moves to the new Review heading when a build finishes or fails, not only when the screen changes.

### Data and control flow

```text
Paste slot ──► validatePasteBatch (main)
  ──► valid | order_error | invalid + exact message
  ──► SlotBadge + SlotError (renderer)

Build ──► reportStarted ──► Review
  ──► progress events ──► ReviewProgress (scored/total + progress + Cancel)
  ──► Cancel ──► reportCancel

Result
  ──► ok: VerdictLine (verdict + unscored note) → Timeline → bands → games → AI
  ──► refusal: RefusalPanel (reason heading + metrics + remedy) → Timeline trace
  ──► error: Report unavailable panel with the one-sentence failure

Edit games ──► flow.draft retained ──► Games
```

### Where it changed

- `src/renderer/PasteValidation.tsx`, `src/renderer/PasteValidation.test.ts`: per-slot badge and exact error line.
- `src/renderer/PasteScreen.tsx`: uses the extracted validation components.
- `src/renderer/ReviewProgress.tsx`, `src/renderer/ReviewProgress.test.ts`: progress text, native progress element, Cancel states.
- `src/renderer/RefusalPanel.tsx`, `src/renderer/RefusalPanel.test.ts`: reason heading, coverage numbers, remedy.
- `src/renderer/VerdictLine.test.ts`: verdict-first markup and unscored-position copy.
- `src/shared/timeline.ts`, `src/shared/timeline.test.ts`: `refusalHeading`.
- `src/renderer/Timeline.tsx`: refusal summary removed; trace rendering unchanged.
- `src/renderer/App.tsx`: Review uses the new components, adopts an opened session id, and moves focus when a build finishes or fails.
- `package.json`, `tsconfig.renderer-test.json`: the new markup tests.

## Post-W4 review fixes

The review pass against `a4e7921` was checked finding by finding; only still-valid issues were changed.

### Fixed

- **Grounding whitespace:** direct-claim matching normalizes runs of whitespace to one space before the pattern loop, while `groundInsight` still returns the original text. Newline and tab claim cases were added, plus a measured-pulse newline acceptance case.
- **Mate distance:** `mateToCp` floors a long mate at 5,000 instead of decaying to 100, so a mate in 100 still outranks a normal centipawn score. Short-mate values and the sign are unchanged; a long-mate test was added.
- **Null-CPL fixture:** the metrics test helper now preserves an explicit `null` `cpl`/`accuracy` instead of replacing it with a default, so the mate aggregation test actually receives null CPL.
- **Engine restart allowance:** replacement spawns now count in `evaluateAttempt` at spawn time and the engine-wide allowance is checked there. A later evaluation cannot get a fresh worker after the budget is spent. A cross-evaluation regression test was added.
- **Camera admission:** `sessionStarting` reserves the camera before `preview.stop`, preview admission is rejected while it is set, and the controller runs a consent/busy guard inside its serialized queue immediately before native capture. Concurrent `sessionStart` calls now get a typed `session_busy`.
- **Delete versus build:** session deletion rejects an active build with `session_busy`, then performs the folder removal under the report exclusion so a build that starts after the check cannot recreate artifacts.
- **Log bounds and redaction:** one oversized record is truncated to the file cap with an explicit marker; JSON-escaped secret forms are redacted on write and read; secrets are collected before directory creation so console redaction survives a failed file sink.
- **Saved-session hand-off:** opening a session invalidates the previous report request sequence, cancels a build in progress, clears insight, adopts the new session id, and the reducer refuses `openedSession` while a live session exists. `reportReady` rejects a report from a different review session.
- **Session-row date:** a finite timestamp that still produces an invalid `Date` returns “Unknown date.”
- **Session confirmation focus:** Delete/Export confirmation moves focus to Cancel and restores it to the initiating button. A DOM interaction test remains NOT_RUN until S57.
- **AI privacy copy:** the explainer no longer claims that all data stays local. It says measured video/images/pulse stay local, and the optional AI reading sends the question, pasted games, and summary numbers to the configured provider.

### Verified already correct, no change

- **Engine packaging:** `engine-worker.ts` selects `stockfish('lite-single')`, which loads `stockfish-19-lite-single.js/.wasm`; those files are not excluded in `package.json`. The excluded variants are the ones not selected.
- **Engine restart claim:** the previous code already kept the allowance engine-wide, but the spawn-time enforcement above closes the later-evaluation gap.
- **Diagnostics:** `doctor`'s AI row is `readAiConfig` only; it makes no provider call and never includes the key or a provider error. Doctor lines contain no secret values to redact.
- **IPC sender:** the app loads only its own file/dev page; navigation is denied, `frame-src 'none'`, the renderer is sandboxed, and no remote document or subframe can reach IPC. A sender check would be redundant.
- **Native runtime order:** the compiled `dist-electron/main/index.js` starts with `require("./native-runtime.js")` before the capture/SDK imports.
- **Preview stop rejection:** `CaptureSession.stop()` catches stop/destroy failures and resolves after attempting `destroy`, so the controller's cleared ownership is safe.
- **Stopping snapshot:** a manual stop publishes no terminal event, so reporting a stopping reservation as live would strand a reloaded page on an unusable Sensing screen. A new start waits on `stoppingSession`, and the stored session is available from Sessions.
- **Setup IPC test loading:** the test suite loads `setup-ipc` and `ipc-registry` successfully under the configured runtime; no boundary change was needed.

### What was done and why

A report build no longer deletes the previous report before it knows that a replacement is valid. Invalid PGNs, low-coverage refusals, and other pre-write failures leave the previous `report.json` and `games.json` untouched.

Every new report now carries `gamesDigest`: lowercase SHA-256 over the UTF-8 encoding of `JSON.stringify(pgns)`, where `pgns` is the exact ordered string array saved to `games.json`. The schema requires the digest, so an older report without one is stale rather than silently accepted.

Before AI configuration or a provider call, `requestInsight` recomputes the digest from the supplied stored PGNs and compares it with the report. A missing or mismatched digest returns rebuild guidance and makes zero fetch calls. The paired IPC reads still run under `withReportExclusion`.

### Data and control flow

```text
buildReport
  ──► read session + samples
  ──► coverage/PGN/alignment/engine work
  ──► reportSchema.parse({ gamesDigest: digestGames(pgns), ... })
  ──► saveGames(games.json)
  ──► saveReport(report.json)

Failure before either save
  ──► previous report.json and games.json remain byte-identical

AI reading
  ──► readReport + readGames under report exclusion
  ──► reportSchema validates required gamesDigest
  ──► digestGames(storedPgns) === report.gamesDigest
  ──► only then read AI configuration or call a provider
```

### Where it changed

- `src/main/report.ts`: removed the early delete and stamps each valid report with the PGN digest.

## S57 — Test infrastructure (BUG-30, BUG-29)

**State:** PARTIAL, UNCOMMITTED on `hardening` above `fb43ba2`. H-29: test discovery and single-source CSP PASS. Renderer DOM tests and the Electron end-to-end suite are NOT_RUN until the dev dependencies below are approved and installed.

### What was done and why

`npm test` no longer carries a hand-written list of compiled files. `scripts/test-files.mjs` walks `dist-electron/**/*.test.js`, `dist-renderer-test/**/*.test.js`, and `scripts/*.test.mjs`; `scripts/run-tests.mjs` runs the discovered files through `node:test` and compares the number of files that emitted test events with the number discovered. A compiled file that registers no tests fails the run instead of passing silently. A missing compiled root fails with a message that names the TypeScript build.

The runner uses the `node:test` programmatic `run()` API rather than spawning `node --test`: each event carries the file that produced it, which is what makes the file-count comparison possible. The built-in `spec` reporter still formats the output, so the console looks like the previous run.

The CSP now lives in one TypeScript file. `vite.config.mts` imports `src/shared/security.ts` directly (Vite bundles its config, so no JavaScript duplicate is needed), and `src/shared/security.mjs` is deleted. `security.test.ts` asserts that the Vite config names the `.ts` source, that no `.mjs` duplicate exists, and that the compiled policy matches the source.

### Data and control flow

```text
npm test
  ──► tsc -p tsconfig.node.json
  ──► tsc -p tsconfig.renderer-test.json
  ──► node scripts/run-tests.mjs
        ──► discoverTestFiles(cwd)
        ──► run({ files })
        ──► collect event.data.file for every test event
        ──► print "Ran M of N test files"
        ──► exit 1 if M < N or any test failed

npm run build
  ──► vite.config.mts imports src/shared/security.ts
  ──► transformIndexHtml replaces __CHESSPULSE_CSP__
```

### Where it changed

- `scripts/test-files.mjs`, `scripts/test-files.test.mjs`: discovery, sort, dedupe, and missing-root behaviour.
- `scripts/run-tests.mjs`: the test entry point and the ran/discovered count check.
- `package.json`: `test` becomes the two `tsc` runs plus `node scripts/run-tests.mjs`.
- `vite.config.mts`: imports the TypeScript CSP source.
- `src/shared/security.mjs`: deleted.
- `src/shared/security.test.ts`: compiled-policy check and single-source guard.

### Verification

Tested state: uncommitted S57 diff on `hardening`, base `fb43ba2`, local Node 22.22.1, 2026-11-22.

- `npm run typecheck`: PASS, Electron and renderer TypeScript projects.
- `npm test`: PASS, 450/450 tests in 96 suites, `Discovered 54 test files` and `Ran 54 of 54 test files`.
- `npm run build`: PASS, TypeScript plus Vite renderer and preload bundles.
- CSP comparison: PASS, the `dist/index.html` CSP attribute was byte-identical before and after removing `security.mjs`. The pre-change build was captured immediately before the edit.
- `git diff --check`: PASS.

### What to understand and be able to explain

The test list is now derived from build output, so adding `foo.test.ts` and rebuilding is enough for it to run. The count comparison is the safety net: a file that compiles but never calls `test()` would otherwise contribute zero tests and look like a pass.

The CSP duplicate existed only because Vite's config loader once needed plain JavaScript. Vite bundles its config with esbuild, which reads TypeScript directly, so the duplicate was pure drift risk. One file, one policy, and a test that points at the importer.

### Limitations and next work

- Renderer DOM tests still need a DOM implementation; the Electron end-to-end suite still needs an Electron launcher. The exact dependency list is waiting for approval before install. Until then H-27's focus/keyboard claims and the real reload path remain unverified in a DOM.
- The runner assumes the `tsc` projects produced their outputs; it does not compile by itself.
- W5 has no written sections in this file; see the documentation gap at the top.

Consequences: a reload no longer contradicts main, and a late hydration cannot replace a session the page already adopted, finished, or is reviewing. The location in `src/shared` is a test seam for the current Node-only test build, not a shared main contract. The snapshot deliberately omits stored samples, so a reloaded strip refills from new batches and the stored trace is untouched. A session that is starting reports closed in the snapshot but is adopted from the start event; a session already stopping also reports closed, because a user stop has no terminal event and a reloaded page must not show an unusable Stop control. Focus movement is implemented but not DOM-tested until S57; S55 still owns the keyboard audit that closes BUG-12.

## 2026-11-22 — Keep the explainer preference in page storage and test markup without a DOM runner

Context: S47 needs the first-run explainer to appear once, be reopenable from Help, and pass heading and list checks. The plan names renderer tests, but no DOM test runner is installed; S57 owns that dependency decision. A main-process preference file would add an IPC path and disk writes for a cosmetic flag.

Options for the preference: a main-process preferences file; a session-style store entry; or page `localStorage` behind a safe wrapper. For the tests: defer all renderer checks to S57; add jsdom/testing-library early; or render the component to static markup with the already-installed `react-dom/server`.

Choice: the preference is `localStorage["chesspulse.explainer.seen.v1"]`, read once in the reducer's lazy initializer, written best-effort before dismissal. A missing, blocked, or throwing store reads as not seen. Markup checks run through a small `tsconfig.renderer-test.json` project that compiles only `Explainer` and its copy module and asserts headings, `<ol>`, `aria-current`, the text marker, and the never-does list with `renderToStaticMarkup`.

Consequences: clearing site data or blocking storage re-shows the explainer, which is the safe failure because it restates consent and fair-play limits. Dev-server and packaged `file://` origins keep separate preferences. Static markup proves structure and copy, not focus, live regions, or the click-to-dismiss path; those stay NOT_RUN until S57, and S55 still owns the keyboard audit. No dependency was added, and S57 can replace this with a full DOM runner without changing the component.

## 2026-11-22 — Add a preview-only capture mode and derive framing from one SDK code

Context: S48 closes BUG-20. Framing advice lived only in the README, Start could open a session that measures nothing, and the page had no camera until a session existed. Opening a session just to frame would store a session before the player chose one. The SDK exposes one current validation code, not three independent booleans.

Options for framing: add a separate preview camera in the page; open a real session early; or reuse the main-process capture pipeline with the sample sink removed. For the checks: infer three booleans from the latest image, or map the SDK's current code to the three checks.

Choice: a serialized preview controller in main runs the same SmartSpectra capture with `onSamples` discarded and no session files, publishes only preview frames and validation hints, and is stopped before any session starts. Preview start requires consent, the key, no open session, and no stop in flight. `framingFromValidation` maps the current code to face/chest/light and leaves the rest unknown; only the SDK `ok` code passes all three. `setupGate` checks consent, key, preview, then framing, and Start has no override. The key row is the doctor's `sensing-key` result.

Consequences: the camera opens during Setup after consent, which is a deliberate, visible framing aid rather than a recording. No sample, session header, report, or PGN is written by preview. A partial or unknown validation code disables Start, which can look stricter than the image; that is the point, because the SDK has not confirmed a measurable frame. The controller serializes start/stop so StrictMode and quick navigation cannot fight over the native device, and a stop in flight counts as owning the camera for quit. The live camera path remains unproven until the user runs Setup with a real key and camera; the controller, gate, and markup are the tested parts.

## 2026-11-22 — Show a page clock and a trailing-minute quality reading, and count marks in main

Context: S49 closes BUG-10, BUG-16, and BUG-17. The page had no elapsed time, no limit warning, no quality reading, no visible gap state, and Stop ended a session on one click. The page has no monotonic clock shared with main, and a renderer reload could otherwise lose the player-marked game count.

Options for the clock: add a shared monotonic value to every event, or display wall-clock elapsed from the stored start. For quality: rate the whole session, or the trailing minute. For the count: keep it only in the reducer, or keep it in the coach and carry it in the reload snapshot.

Choice: elapsed is `Date.now() - startedAtEpochMs`, refreshed once a second; the header and main's timer remain authoritative. Quality is the usable-sample share of the 60 seconds ending at the newest sample, with a separate five-second stale check. The 80-minute warning derives from the same elapsed value. The coach owns `markedGames`, increments only on a false-to-true gap transition, and `cp:app:state` carries it; the reducer mirrors the same transition. Stop is an inline confirmation with Keep sensing focused and Escape cancelling.

Consequences: a wall-clock change can move the displayed warning without moving the real stop, which is visible in the UI but not in the stored duration. Quality does not invent a stale "good" reading after the stream stops. The game count survives a renderer reload while the session is live and cannot be inflated by repeats or inference. The confirmation is non-modal and has no focus trap, which is honest for an inline panel but means focus can leave it; S55 rechecks keyboard behavior.

## 2026-11-22 — Make the stored session list tolerant and keep games reachable from a broken report

Context: S50 closes BUG-08 and BUG-32. Earlier sessions existed but were unreachable; the index and headers could contain a folder that no longer parsed; and a stale, newer, or invalid report would otherwise block the original PGNs. The list needs a date, duration, coverage, and report presence for each row without opening every report.

Options for an unreadable session: fail the whole list, silently drop it, or count it. For the report badge: parse every report, or check that the file exists. For opening: require a valid report, or fall back to Games with a reason.

Choice: `listSessionSummaries` reads each header independently, counts a failing folder as `unreadable`, sorts newest first, and uses a `report.json` existence check for the badge. `openStoredSession` treats `missing` as no report; `stale`, `newer`, and `invalid` become a named reason while the stored PGNs are still returned, so Open lands on Games. Delete refuses the currently running session in main, not only in the renderer. Delete and export both require an inline row confirmation.

Consequences: one corrupt folder cannot hide the rest, and the list stays cheap because it does not parse reports. "Report saved" is honest but weaker than "report valid"; opening performs the real check and never traps the player without the games. A corrupt `games.json` is treated as no stored PGNs, not a separate error. Export still chooses its path in the native dialog and remains untested in a real UI run.

## 2026-11-22 — Let Review own refusal presentation and keep paste state in the reducer

Context: S51 closes H-23. Paste errors and illegal moves were already produced in main, but the per-slot message had no renderer test because it lived inside the bridge-bound Paste screen. Refusal copy was split between a generic Timeline panel and the Review heading, so the real reason and the remedy were not guaranteed to appear together. Progress and Cancel lived inside App and had no focused test. Opened sessions also did not update the renderer's session id, so progress could be ignored.

Options for refusals: keep the generic Timeline panel, duplicate the reason in both places, or move the summary to Review and let Timeline draw only the trace. For pasted text: keep it in the form, lift it to the reducer, or refetch it from disk on every back.

Choice: `PasteValidation` owns the badge and exact error line; `RefusalPanel` owns the reason heading, coverage metrics, and builder remedy; `Timeline` no longer prints a refusal summary. `ReviewProgress` owns progress and Cancel. The paste draft stays in `flow.draft`, updated on every edit and on open. Opening a stored session sets the renderer's current session id before the result is dispatched, so progress events and insight calls use it. Review focus moves when the build state changes.

Consequences: the refusal reason and remedy have one renderer owner and cannot drift from the Timeline, and the real illegal-move message is testable without a bridge. The paste survives every back path; only a new session clears it. The build and Cancel remain untested against a real minutes-long Stockfish run, and the refusal heading is fixed copy until S56.

## 2026-11-22 — Close post-W4 review gaps in admission, restarts, logs, and saved-session hand-off

Context: A review of `a4e7921` raised packaging, grounding, metrics, diagnostics, engine, camera, IPC, log, preview, session, renderer, and copy findings. Some were already correct; others were real races or claims.

Choice: mate scores floor at 5,000; the metrics fixture preserves null; claim matching normalizes whitespace but returns the original text; engine replacement spawns are counted at spawn time and bounded across evaluations; `sessionStarting` plus a controller-internal guard serializes camera admission and rechecks consent before native capture; session delete rejects an in-flight build and runs under the report exclusion; logs truncate one record to the cap, redact JSON-escaped secrets, and collect secrets before directory creation; opening a saved session invalidates outstanding report requests and resets insight; the reducer rejects a live-session replacement and a mismatched report result; session dates reject invalid `Date`s; the explainer states the optional AI payload accurately.

Consequences: long mates stay decisive; a spent worker allowance cannot reset on the next evaluation; a preview cannot start after consent withdrawal or during a reserved session start; a delete cannot pair with a build that recreates artifacts; a log record cannot exceed the cap; a saved session cannot be overwritten by a late result from the previous one. The session-row focus interaction test and the live Electron paths remain NOT_RUN until S57/S59. The review's packaging, diagnostics, IPC-sender, native-order, preview-stop, stopping-snapshot, and setup-test findings were verified correct and left unchanged.

content.text:
**Where we are:** W6 / S57 — test infrastructure and one CSP source. Implemented and verified, uncommitted on `hardening` above `fb43ba2`.

**What changed**
- `scripts/run-tests.mjs` discovers compiled tests from `dist-electron`, `dist-renderer-test`, and top-level `scripts/*.test.mjs`; prints `Discovered N` / `Ran M of N`; fails if a discovered file registers no tests.
- `vite.config.mts` now imports `src/shared/security.ts` directly; `security.mjs` is deleted and guarded by a test.
- Added the approved dev dependencies only: `jsdom@29.1.1`, `@types/jsdom@30.0.0`, `playwright-core@1.65.1`.
- `src/renderer/dom-harness.ts` plus DOM tests for the two previously unproven focus paths: Stop confirmation (`SensingControls`) and delete/export confirmation (`SessionList`).
- `scripts/e2e/electron.test.mjs` launches the built app through `_electron` with isolated `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, and checks first-run, Skip, Tab to “Start a session”, Help → Back, reload, CSP meta tag, and a second launch.

**Verify**
- `npm run typecheck`: **PASS**
- `npm test`: **PASS** — 458/458 tests, 98 suites, 56/56 files
- `npm run test:e2e`: **PASS twice consecutively** — 1/1 each run
- `npm run build`: **PASS**
- CSP before/after `security.mjs` removal: **byte-identical**
- `git diff --check`: **PASS**
- BUG-29 and BUG-30: **Closed** with evidence.

**What this means:** A new test file can no longer be silently skipped, and the test run now proves its own coverage by file count. The duplicated CSP is gone without changing the built policy. Focus and keyboard behaviour that used to be “reviewed by eye” now has a real DOM and Electron test behind it.

**One incident, fixed:** The first E2E run used only `XDG_DATA_HOME`, so Chromium wrote the explainer preference into your real `~/.config/chesspulse` profile. I added `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` isolation and reset that one key to its previous state (`null`). Repeated E2E runs now leave no trace.

**Docs updated:** `docs/phases/phase-05.md` (S57 section, phase state, documentation-gap note), `docs/phases/phase-05-bugs.md` (BUG-29/30 closed, stale BUG-32 row corrected), `docs/decisions.md` (test discovery, dependency, and CSP decision).

**Two honest gaps outside W6:**
- `phase-05.md` has no written S52–S56 sections even though W5 is committed; S60 will have to reconstruct H-24–H-28 evidence rather than assume it.
- H-27’s “keyboard map shown with `?`” does not exist anywhere in the renderer. That is a W5/S55 defect, not something I changed during W6.

**Next step:** S58 — the written bug-bash script across every §3.1 flow and §3.5 error, run on the built app. Say the word and I’ll start it; W6 still commits only once, after S60, with your explicit instruction naming W6.

---README---
# ChessPulse

ChessPulse is a local desktop app for reviewing a chess.com session after you play. It keeps a pulse trace beside the clock and the moves, then asks whether a bad stretch was a state problem or a chess problem.

It is not a chess trainer, not an engine overlay, and not a medical device. It makes no diagnosis.

The app does not watch a rated game. There is no engine, evaluation, or advice while a game is live. You play on chess.com. ChessPulse looks at the session afterwards.

## Run

Requirements: Node 22, npm, a display, and a camera for sensing.

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env
npm test
npm run dev
```

`npm test` is the unit suite. `npm run test:consent` is separate: it builds `dist/` and `dist-electron/` first, then opens Electron. It is not part of `npm test` and does not run without that build.

`npm run dev` opens the window against the local page at `http://127.0.0.1:5173`. `npm run build` then `npm start` opens the built page from disk.

If Electron aborts because the sandbox helper is not setuid, start the built app with `--no-sandbox`. That flag is a development workaround.

```bash
npx electron --no-sandbox .
```

The SmartSpectra key and any model key belong in `.env` only. `.env.example` lists the names and stays empty. The main process reads `.env` at startup; a value already exported by the shell wins. Sensing needs `SMARTSPECTRA_API_KEY`; the window does not call a model.

## Consent and data

The camera stays off until you press **Allow the camera**. Revoking consent releases the camera and stops an open session. The main process opens the camera through the SmartSpectra SDK and does all measuring there; the page receives a small preview bitmap and the measured numbers, never the key. Nothing is recorded.

A session folder contains `meta.json`, `samples.ndjson`, and—after a review—`games.json` with the original PGNs and `report.json` with computed results. No image or video file is written. The folder is under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/chesspulse` or `~/.local/share/chesspulse`. Deleting that folder deletes the session. Sensing and local report building upload nothing, and there is no account.

If you configure an AI provider and choose **Write reading**, that provider receives your question, the original PGNs, and computed summary numbers. It never receives video or the raw pulse trace. The response is shown as untrusted `INFERRED` text and does not change the report. Without an AI key, the panel explains that it is disabled and makes no request.

## Current limits

The sensing screen draws pulse samples as the session stores them, and breaks the line when samples are more than one second apart. It also shows a mirrored camera preview and the measured light level.

Framing matters more than anything else. The player must be the only face in frame, facing the camera, with the **upper chest visible** — the SDK reports "Place more of the chest in view" and produces no pulse until that is true. Sit back until your shoulders and chest are in the preview. In a dim room the preview is brightened for framing only; the measured frames are unchanged, so a genuinely dark room still lowers confidence and coverage. A lamp in front of you is the fix.

The capture path has not yet been verified against a real seated session reporting usable coverage. Without a camera or a valid key, starting a session stops with the specific reason (no camera, rejected key, no credit, network failure). Pulse, not breathing, is the only metric requested.

After a game ends, press **Game ended**. If the trailing-minute median of usable pulse samples is at least 10 bpm above your baseline, one coach line shows the measured figures and suggests a break. Press **Next game started** before playing again; this removes the line. A real threshold crossing has not yet been captured.

Pasted games, local Stockfish scoring, the report, the between-games coach, and the optional AI reading panel are in this build. The panel's provider access and real response quality have not yet been verified.

# Phase 5 bug bash — S58

Built app, isolated profile, local Node 22.22.1, 2026-11-22. The automated half is
`scripts/e2e/bug-bash.mjs` (`npm run test:bash`). Screenshots go to `docs/images/bug-bash/`.

The bash uses two profiles:

- **Fresh profile** — no sessions, an empty `.env` file so Setup sees a missing key. No camera is
  opened and no provider is called.
- **Seeded profile** — a copy of a real captured session with pulse samples (contract: read-only
  copy of `$XDG_DATA_HOME/chesspulse/sessions`, never the original). Its coverage is below the
  70% gate, so a pasted game must produce a refusal, not a report. The pasted PGNs are the real
  chess.com PGNs in `docs/proofs/s4/`; they are not presented as belonging to that session. The
  coverage gate refuses before alignment, so no verdict or band can be mistaken for evidence.

## §3.1 flows

| Flow | Steps | Expected | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Home, first run | Launch with no preference | Explainer heading, five steps, three limits, Start setup and Skip for now; no controls behind it | PENDING |
| Home, returning | Skip the explainer | "Ready when you are.", Start a session, All sessions, Help, empty recent-sessions message | PENDING |
| Help | Open from Home and from Sessions | Help heading, explainer at heading level 2, Copy diagnostics, Back returns to the opener | PENDING |
| Sessions, empty | All sessions with no stored sessions | "No sessions yet. Start one from Home." | PENDING |
| Setup, blocked | Start a session with no key and no consent | Start sensing disabled; consent reason first, then the missing-key sentence; key value never shown | PENDING |
| Setup, consent | Allow the camera, then reload and return to Setup | Consent persists; Start still blocked by the missing key; camera never opens | PENDING |
| Sessions, one row | Seeded profile | Date, duration, coverage, "No report yet"; Open and Delete enabled, Export disabled with a reason | PENDING |
| Open a session without a report | Open from the row | Games screen with three empty paste slots | PENDING |
| Games, invalid PGN | Paste text that is not a PGN | "Needs fix", the slot marked invalid, Continue disabled | PENDING |
| Games, real PGN | Paste `10+0.pgn` | Slot valid, clocks present, "No timestamps" order note, Continue enabled | PENDING |
| Games, illegal move | Replace the first SAN with an illegal move | "Game 1, move 1 (e5) is not legal", Continue disabled | PENDING |
| Review, low coverage | Continue with a valid game on the 1%-coverage session | "Review withheld.", measured coverage and the 70% threshold, the remedy, trace, and all exit actions | PENDING |
| Delete confirmation | Delete on a row | Confirmation copy, Cancel focused; Cancel returns focus to Delete; nothing deleted | PENDING |
| Export without a report | Export on a row | Disabled; no dialog, no confirmation | PENDING |
| Keyboard | Tab through Home and Setup | Every visible control reachable in order; focus visible; no trap | PENDING |

## §3.5 errors and empty states

| Error | How exercised | Expected | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| No key | Fresh profile with an empty env file | "Missing. Set SMARTSPECTRA_API_KEY in .env or the environment." and the same sentence as the Start reason | PENDING |
| Illegal move | Modified real PGN | Game, full move number, and SAN in one sentence | PENDING |
| PGN without EndTime | Real `10+0.pgn` | Order marked unverified, with the one-line explanation; not a silent guess | PENDING |
| Low coverage | Seeded 1% session | Refusal with measured %, threshold, and remedy; no verdict, bands, or saved report | PENDING |
| Empty sessions list | Fresh profile | Plain empty message, no fake row | PENDING |
| Camera refused | Needs a camera attempt | — | NOT_RUN — the bash does not open the camera |
| Rejected key / no credit / network during sensing | Needs a real SDK start | — | NOT_RUN — S59, user-run |
| AI rejected key / rate limit / provider failure | Needs a paid provider call | — | NOT_RUN — S59, user-run |
| Successful report | Needs a session at or above 70% coverage | — | NOT_RUN — S59, user-run |

## Defects found

Recorded in `docs/phases/phase-05-bugs.md` after the run. The phase cannot close with an open P0
or P1 from this bash.

## 1. Real seated session at 70% coverage or more

Why: proves the product does the job on real hardware, not only on the refusal path.

Setup:

- One face, upper chest visible, a lamp in front, no other face in frame.
- `SMARTSPECTRA_API_KEY` in `.env`. No AI key is needed for this run.

Steps:

1. Home → Start a session → Allow the camera. Wait until all three framing checks pass.

4. Paste the PGNs oldest first; build the report.

  ──► npm run build in the copy
  ──► launch with CHESSPULSE_ENV_FILE and a separate XDG_DATA_HOME

**State:** DRAFTED, NOT CLOSED, NOT COMMITTED. The final commands pass and the register is resolved, but five checks remain `NOT_RUN` and W5 is not actually complete. This section records the evidence rather than asserting a close.

### What Phase 5 changed

- **W1 (data safety).** A failed or refused build leaves the previous report and games byte-identical; report and PGN files are digest-paired; a two-file save is staged and renamed; storage failures and the 90-minute limit end one session with one reason.
- **W2 (scoring correctness).** Mate scores are scaled so a forced mate is not a blunder; illegal moves are found at paste time with game, move, and SAN; engine timeouts, crashes, cancellation, and the engine-wide restart budget are counted; positions are scored through linear indexes; coach memory is time-bounded.
- **W3 (backend).** Every IPC handler ends in a typed code; the page never prints raw internal text; logs redact key values by value; the diagnostics bundle carries metadata and doctor lines only; the store has a schema gate, index repair, delete, and export; the Linux AppImage builds.
- **W4 (flow).** Home, Setup, Sensing, Stopped, Games, Review, Sessions, and Help are one reducer-owned flow; reload restores consent and the live session; the first-run explainer is stored locally; Start is gated on consent, key, preflight, and framing; sessions open, delete, and export; paste state survives back paths.
- **W5 (UI system).** Tokens, a contrast script, component classes, ending-label spacing, reduced-motion rules, and a copy check exist. The workstream was committed early; the component/copy/keyboard deliverables are only partly present (below).
- **W6 (verification).** Tests are discovered from build output; renderer DOM tests and a built-app Electron suite exist; the CSP has one source; the bug bash covers every reachable flow and error; evidence tooling and a short-limit build are prepared.

**Primary action and hierarchy.** One action per screen. On the report: the verdict line first,
then the timeline, then numbers by band, then the AI reading. Nothing competes with the verdict
line — it is the only place the page raises its voice.

**Character.** A lab readout: calm, clinical, unpatronising. No confetti, streaks, emoji, gamified
copy, or motivational reassurance. Numbers are stated, not celebrated.

**Palette** — one accent, reserved exclusively for the elevated state.

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `--bg` | `#0E1012` | App background (graphite, not black) |
| `--surface` | `#161A1D` | Panels |
| `--line` | `#262C31` | Hairlines, chart grid |
| `--text` | `#E9E7E3` | Primary text (warm off-white) |
| `--muted` | `#98A0A6` | Labels, secondary |
| `--accent` | `#E0663A` | **Elevated state only** — never buttons, never links, never decoration |
| `--ok` | `#6F8F7B` | Rare: validated, aligned |
| `--warn` | `#C9A227` | Low-confidence and refusals |

Dark by choice: the product is used at night, next to a chess board, and it photographs cleanly in
a 60-second video. One theme only — no light mode in scope.

**Type.** Inter for UI; a tabular-figure monospace (JetBrains Mono) for every number that changes.
Scale 12 / 14 / 16 / 20 / 28 / 40. Spacing 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 24 / 32 / 48. Radii 4 (controls) and
8 (panels). One 1 px border weight.

**Components** (nine, reused everywhere): `ScreenShell`, `ActionButton`, `TimeControlPicker`,
`SensingStrip`, `ValidationHint`, `Timeline`, `BandBars`, `VerdictLine`, `InsightPanel`. Plus
`Refusal` and `ErrorState`, which are copy variants of one component, not new patterns.

### 7.4 Screens and states

| Screen | Purpose | States to design |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Start | time control + consent | default · consent expanded · remembered consent · key missing |
| 2 Sensing | live strip, deliberately sparse | waiting for face · validating · sensing · low confidence · no camera · SDK error |
| 3 Between games | one line | silent (nothing to say) · coach line fired |
| 4 Paste | PGN input and validation | empty · partial (1–2 games) · out of order · clockless · all valid |
| 5 Report | the product | refused (low coverage) · aligned · low-confidence alignment · partial (some games excluded) |
| 6 Reading | AI panels | no key · thinking · ready · provider error |

### 7.5 Real copy

These are the strings Prompt 2 types in. Numbers shown are shape-illustrative; the app prints the
computed ones.

**Verdict line** — pure function, no model involved:

> *8 blunders, 5 of them in the eleven minutes your pulse stayed 18 bpm above baseline. Accuracy
> 71% settled, 54% elevated. Between games 2 and 3 you waited four minutes and never came down.*

Template: `{blunders} blunders, {n} of them in {span} your pulse stayed {delta} bpm above baseline.
Accuracy {settled}% settled, {elevated}% elevated. {gapClause}` — with `gapClause` omitted when no
gap qualifies.

**Coach line** (between games): *Pulse still +19 over baseline. You queued here last time and
lost.*

## 2026-11-22 — Finish W5 with a small component vocabulary, one copy module, and a real keyboard map

For copy: move every string into a renderer module while leaving domain messages in their shared modules; or move every layer's strings into one file.
